All premises related to the SOD1 gene are established. 

SOD1 mutations contribute to familial amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) primarily through a gain-of-function mechanism. Mutations in the SOD1 gene can lead to the production of a misfolded protein that aggregates, resulting in toxic effects on motor neurons. This misfolding can disrupt cellular processes, lead to oxidative stress, and ultimately result in neuronal death. Additionally, the accumulation of these aggregates can trigger inflammatory responses and further contribute to neurodegeneration. 

In summary, SOD1 mutations are linked to familial ALS through mechanisms involving protein misfolding, aggregation, and neurotoxicity.
